draft.title: Derivatives of trigonometric functions
card: With x in radians: the derivative of sin x is cos x, of cos x is −sin x, and of tan x is sec²x. Here sec x means 1/cos x.
If the angle is a function, use the chain rule. Differentiate the trig function, keep the inside the same, then multiply by the derivative of the inside.
So d/dx [sin(f(x))] = f'(x) cos(f(x)), and d/dx [cos(f(x))] = −f'(x) sin(f(x)). For tan, d/dx [tan(f(x))] = f'(x) sec²(f(x)).
y = sin(3x). The inside is 3x, and its derivative is 3. So dy/dx = 3cos(3x).
draft.remember: Differentiate the trig function, keep the inside, then multiply by the derivative of the inside.

a.q: What is the derivative of cos(5x)?
a.why: The derivative of cos is −sin, and the inside 5x has derivative 5. So the answer is −5sin(5x). Leaving out the minus sign gives 5sin(5x), which is a common sign error.
a.clue: The derivative of cos has a minus sign, and the inside also adds a factor.

b.q: What is the gradient of y = tan(2x) at x = 0?
b.why: dy/dx = 2sec²(2x). At x = 0, sec²(0) = 1/cos²(0) = 1, so the gradient is 2 × 1 = 2. The answer 1 comes from forgetting to multiply by the derivative of 2x.
b.clue: Use the chain rule first, then put x = 0 into sec².
